content.company_name: Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock
content.answer_markdown: **Answer:** Crescent Energy Company Class A common stock (CRGY) is an Eagle Ford oil and gas producer. The October 2026 purchase of Devon Energy's Eagle Ford assets and the $1 billion share sale explain the recent price weakness. The facts give no clear edge for the next week or month. For three to twelve months, the facts lean slightly bullish, but that lean depends on how Crescent pays for the $4.2 billion deal and on third-quarter results. **Company and catalyst:** CRGY is Crescent Energy Company Class A common stock (SEC CIK 1866175), focused on the Eagle Ford shale in Texas ([Crescent Energy operations](https://crescentenergyco.com/operations/default.aspx)). On 2026-10-08, Devon Energy agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent for $4.2 billion in cash, covering about 90,000 net acres ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/devon-energy-sell-eagle-ford-assets-crescent-energy-42-billion-2026-10-08/); [Oil & Gas Journal](https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/companies/news/55410522/crescent-energy-to-acquire-eagle-ford-assets-from-devon-for-42-billion)). One report cites about $140 million in annual synergies, meaning cost savings ([Zacks via TradingView](https://fr.tradingview.com/news/zacks:4642dd455094b:0-crescent-energy-s-devon-deal-strengthens-its-eagle-ford-dominance/)). On 2026-10-09, Crescent priced 80 million Class A shares at $12.50 each to raise about $1 billion; a KKR affiliate bought 40 million of those shares ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CRGY/crescent-energy-company-announces-pricing-of-public-offering-of-omfbd0521ooo.html)). The $1 billion covers roughly a quarter of the $4.2 billion purchase price. The disclosed evidence does not say how Crescent will fund the rest. **Price move:** As of 2026-10-14, CRGY fell 1.0% that day, 3.0% over one week, and 12.2% over one month. Over three months it is up 30.1%, and over one year it is up 49.9%. The recent weakness overlaps the deal announcement and the share sale. **Business facts:** For the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026), revenue was $1.395 billion, net income was $492.8 million, operating cash flow was $944.0 million, and free cash flow was $622.0 million. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for capital spending. In the prior quarter (Q1 2026), revenue was $1.183 billion, net income was a loss of $419.8 million, and free cash flow was negative $155.8 million. This large swing shows that earnings change a lot from quarter to quarter. **Bullish case:** Crescent adds acreage next to its existing Eagle Ford position. The $140 million in stated cost savings can raise cash flow. Q2 2026 free cash flow of $622 million shows the business can generate cash. KKR's participation in the share sale is part of the bullish case. This case assumes oil prices hold, the cost savings appear, and Crescent does not need to sell more shares. It would be invalidated by another share sale, a weak Q3 2026 report, or lower oil prices. **Bearish case:** The 80 million new shares dilute existing owners—each existing share now represents a smaller part of the company. If Crescent funds the rest of the $4.2 billion with debt, interest costs rise on top of $6.85 billion in total liabilities. Earnings already swing hard. This case would be invalidated by debt paydown, confirmed cost savings, or a share price recovery above $12.50. **Verdict:** No clear edge at one week to one month. The deal and the share sale create uncertainty, and the recent price drop shows that. At three to twelve months, the facts lean modestly bullish because of the cash flow, the added acreage, and analyst price targets mostly in the $17 to $20 range against the $12.50 offering price. Examples include Wells Fargo at $20 ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/10/62328287/wells-fargo-maintains-overweight-crescent-energy-raises-price-target-20)), UBS at $18 ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/10/62312358/ubs-maintains-buy-crescent-energy-lowers-price-target-18)), Truist at $19 ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/09/61838251/truist-securities-initiates-coverage-crescent-energy-buy-rating-announces-price-target-19)), and Evercore ISI at $17 ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/10/62362360/evercore-isi-group-maintains-outperform-crescent-energy-lowers-price-target-17)). At least one analyst has a sell rating at $12 ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/09/61595918/seaport-global-initiates-coverage-crescent-energy-sell-rating-announces-price-target-12)). The bullish lean depends on facts to obtain. **What to check next:** To decide between the cases, get these facts: (1) how much of the $4.2 billion will be debt and how much equity; (2) the deal's closing date; (3) Q3 2026 production, realised prices, and free cash flow; (4) company confirmation of the roughly $140 million synergy figure.
